title: How to leverage the Kelly Digital Infrastructure Data Center Salary Guide.
summary: Discover how to navigate the booming data center job market with the 2026 Kelly Digital Infrastructure Salary Guide, enhancing hiring strategies and career moves.
body_markdown:
The data center construction boom is causing a massive shift inside multiple labor markets in the United States. Hyperscalers and colocation providers are committing tens of billions of dollars to new campuses in markets that had little to no data center presence five years ago, and every one of those projects needs electricians, controls technicians, network engineers, and facility operators before a single server rack goes live.


That growth has created a strange problem for both sides of the hiring table. Job seekers cannot find reliable numbers on what their skills are worth in a market that barely existed a decade ago. Hiring leaders cannot benchmark offers against a labor pool that is being pulled from construction, manufacturing, telecom, and IT all at once. Job boards show wildly inconsistent ranges, and most compensation data lags a fast-moving market by a year or more.


The


[2026 Kelly Digital Infrastructure Data Center Salary Guide](https://www.kellyservices.com/divisions/digital-infrastructure/salary-guide/data-center/?hsLang=en)


was built to close that gap by benchmarking compensation across more than 50 data center roles while providing insight into the market trends shaping the industry’s future.


Here is how to put the guide to work, whether you are building a hiring strategy or planning your next career move.


[Download the Kelly Digital Infrastructure 2026 Data Center Salary Guide](https://www.kellyservices.com/divisions/digital-infrastructure/salary-guide/data-center/?hsLang=en)


## **Understand market trends before building your hiring strategy.**


##


Salary data only tells part of the story. The guide also tracks the structural shifts reshaping where and how data centers get built, and how those shifts drive compensation just as much as any single role's scarcity.


Some of the topics discussed in the guide include:


-


Where new data center investment is concentrating and why those markets were chosen


-


Which worker profiles are in the highest demand right now, and which are becoming harder to source


-


The most common causes of project delays, many of which trace back to labor and permitting rather than equipment


-


How commissioning timelines are shifting hiring windows earlier in the project lifecycle


Hiring leaders who build their compensation planning around these trends, rather than reacting to them after a project is already behind schedule, consistently land talent faster and at a more predictable cost.


## **Read what's impacting salaries before setting a hiring budget.**


A single "data center salary" figure is close to useless in this market. Compensation swings hard based on which phase of the build a role sits in.


Two organizations hiring for the same role can arrive at very different compensation packages based on project phase, location, workforce availability, certifications, and competing demand in the local market. Understanding those nuances is what turns salary data into a practical workforce planning tool. The guide explains the market forces behind the numbers, not just the numbers themselves.


The guide breaks out the specific drivers behind that range, including:


-


Role scarcity in the local labor market


-


Location and proximity to active buildout corridors


-


Specialized certifications


-


Direct competition from nearby projects hiring for the same skill set


-


24/7 on-call and shift coverage requirements


Pulling benchmarks for the specific role, region, and project phase you are either job seeking or hiring for is what makes the data useful. Knowing the national average isn’t enough with so many different factors at play.


## **Apply expert insights, not just the numbers.**


The biggest differentiator of the 2026 Data Center Salary Guide is that it goes beyond the numbers and provides context from people who staff these projects for a living


The guide is a wealth of knowledge from the people in Kelly Digital Infrastructure who work directly with the operators and general contractors building this infrastructure, and uses that experience to translate their frontline experience into practical guidance.


From identifying adjacent talent pools and understanding hiring timelines to recognizing when traditional recruiting alone is no longer enough, the guide helps organizations think beyond compensation. It also explores strategies like our workforce accelerator program, which helps organizations build job-ready talent pipelines when the local labor market cannot meet demand.


For hiring leaders, that context can mean the difference between setting a compensation package that gets ignored and building a workforce strategy that attracts and develops the right talent. For job seekers, it can mean understanding not just what a role pays, but why demand, location, certifications, and transferable skills influence long-term career opportunities.


## **Put the guide to work.**


[The 2026 Kelly Digital Infrastructure Data Center Salary Guide](https://www.kellyservices.com/divisions/digital-infrastructure/salary-guide/data-center/?hsLang=en)


is built to be used, not just read. Hiring leaders can bring it into compensation planning, offer negotiations, workforce forecasting, and conversations around upcoming projects. Job seekers can use it to better understand their market value, identify in-demand skills and certifications, and prepare for compensation conversations.
